usual_baseline: Anaemia is common and rarely treated. 71% below Hb threshold but 6.7% given iron [2128]; 38% operated with Hb <130 and 7% treated [1387]; iron studies 8% and screening 6 weeks before surgery 3.95% [1590]; 18% of anaemic colorectal patients given IV iron [2046].
fix_that_works: Governance presentation and a departmental plan to treat to Hb 130: operated with Hb <130 fell from 38% to 21%; anaemias investigated 11% to 80% [1387]. Education plus publicising a day-case iron pathway: IV iron 18% to 60%, transfusion 45% to 20% [2046][2174].
fix_that_fails: Actual treatment lagged investigation: attempted treatment rose only from 7% to 20%, not significant (p = 0.279) [1387].
consultant_advice: Everyone finds untreated anaemia. Audit timing instead: whether Hb is checked early enough, at least 6 weeks before surgery, to treat it. Measure iron given and Hb reached, not just screening.
